review_notes: Larson judicial -2/medium: I tested this against the primary refutation, which upheld -1/high and said -2 needed more than restraint statements. The refreshed dossier adds an explicit interpretive rule in his own words: 'Apply the law as written, not as you wish it had been', and the role 'is not to impose ideology' but to apply the law 'as written, consistently' [S3][S4]. Together with the Blake-was-'motivated by ideology' critique [S2], that is the same kind of as-written evidence that places Edwards (Pos 1) at -2, so -2 is consistent across races. Medium is the right hedge, because the as-written wording is campaign-site copy and not repeated across independent interviews as Edwards' is. Larson safety 0/medium is a documented mix, not an unknown. On one side: opposition to proposed bail rules that would 'cripple' trial courts [S2], and the pamphlet's claim that court decisions 'weakened' trial courts' response to crime and addiction [S1]. On the other: six years on the DMCJA Therapeutic Courts Committee [S6] and 'compassion and accountability' collaboration [S1]. One could argue -1, since his stated positions all lean enforcement and the committee is a service role, but therapeutic-court service is sanctioned evidence under the judicial rule, so 0 stands. Larson experience 0/medium and Angelis experience -1/high are fair and consistent with Pos 1 (Melody -1). Angelis judicial and safety are correctly omitted, matching the primary refutation. His statements ('faithfully interpret and apply', 'put aside all policy and political preferences', ruling as 'the law requires' against his own view) are standard judicial language that leans slightly pole_a if anything [S5][S9][S10]. The only pole_b framing is The Stranger's characterization [S12], and his pro bono immigration work is client advocacy. There are no authored opinions [S4]. No basis relies on the WAGOP/Forward Party recommendations or Democratic endorsements. Summary/highlight flags: (1) Angelis's summary says '26 years leading appellate and IP practice at K&L Gates'. The dossier says 26 years at the firm, where he led the appellate practice and was global IP leader [S1][S3]. It does not say he led either one for all 26 years, so '26 years at K&L Gates, where he led the appellate and IP practices' would be accurate. (2) Larson's summary says 'on his fifth Supreme Court run'. The dossier records a source conflict: the Spokesman-Review lists 2000/2016/2020/2024 (fifth run) and the primary record lists 2016/2020/2024 (fourth) [S2][S8]. The summary states one count as fact. Prefer 'his fourth or fifth' or 'after runs in 2016, 2020 and 2024'.
